- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward lower levels after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast for 3–5 days post-peak by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag behind true price movements; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged true values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underreact; increase forecast by 0.5–1% to counteract underestimation.
